messages.author: 7a1a0c66d60b0f26
messages.subject: moving qtl
parts:
Hello everyone,
I am working on a morphological data set that has very good map coverage (344 markers, marker density 3.71±1.66 cM) , genotyping success (99.5%), and 100% phenotyping. I am happy with the multiple QTL models except for one thing - my best model includes 2 loci that are 2 cM apart and when I remove either of them the QTL moves to the next proximal marker and drops significant PVE and LOD scores for the overall model and at single loci. Does anyone have insights into why the variance does not simply move to the other of the 2 neighboring markers rather than being dumped at another altogether? There is no significant interaction between the 2 neighboring loci so it is not a matter of epistatic effect on the overall single locus result either.
Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] moving qtl
parts:
My guess is that the two loci are linked in "repulsion", with effects of opposite sign. When you include just one QTL at that location, the effects of the two loci cancel each other.

The big concern, with such tight QTL, is that the finding may come from just a few individuals with outlying phenotype. I would plot phenotype against the two-locus genotypes.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] moving qtl
parts:
Each of the pair of loci within 2 cM have nearly identical effects on the phenotype. These loci differ in genotype within only 19 individuals, however, within those 19 three are missing gt's at one of the loci and 7 are missing phenotypes. 

Examining the pxg plots it is apparent that both loci (as well as the proximal locus that is given all of the effect when one is removed) have very large phenotypic variations.
